text.p: Fonar Corp, a magnetic resonance imaging company, said on Monday it has been granted a new patent that could potentially lower the cost of medical scans by as much as 50 percent.
In a statement, Fonar said that the new patent on its Quad technology makes simultaneous scanning of up to four patients possible.
It said its new technology can be used on any current type of medical resonance imaging system, most of which have two openings.
It said that its new invention allows an additional one to three beds to a scanner, so that a patent or patients can be positioned and prepared for a scan while another patient is being scanned.
The scanner can thus be used with more patients simultaneously, with little or no down time for patient preparation, it said.
The new invention can be used with a "privacy shield," it said, so each patient can feel he is receiving an individual scan, it said.
Under current systems, usually only about thrpatients can be scanned every hour, with the cost typically ranging from $750 to $1,200 per scan, it said.
With its new patent, it said, as many as twice that number can be scanned every hour.
